claims.claim: A Journal of Prediction Markets study of four real-money movie box-office markets found trading volume and timing consistent with overconfidence, prices consistent with the prior-information equilibrium in three of four markets, significantly higher returns for traders whose forecast matched the winning contract in those three markets, and no significant return differences in the fourth.
claims.episode_span: In three of the four markets, contract prices were consistent with the prior-information equilibrium.
claims.source_title: Private Information, Overconfidence and Trader Returns in Prediction Markets
claims.supporting_quote: In three of the four markets, contract prices were consistent with the prior information equilibrium.

claims.claim: A Journal of Futures Markets study of Sydney Futures Exchange floor locals found significant position-taking profits, positively related to order-flow information and negatively related to exogenous information, liquidity profits, and inventory-cycle length, and characterized locals as active informed traders.
claims.source_title: Local trader profitability in futures markets: Liquidity and position taking profits
claims.supporting_quote: Locals on the trading floor are found to make significant position‐taking profits.

claims.claim: A Journal of Futures Markets study of SSE 50 ETF options found call order imbalances contemporaneously positively associated with underlying returns, put imbalances negatively associated, followed by rapid reversals attributed to market-maker delta-hedging rather than informed trading.
claims.episode_span: Call order imbalances were contemporaneously positively associated with underlying returns, put order imbalances negatively associated, and both were followed by rapid reversals.
claims.source_title: Market Maker or Informed Trader: Who Drive the Relationship Between Option Trading and Underlying Returns? Evidence From Shanghai Stock Exchange 50 ETF Options
claims.supporting_quote: Specifically, call (put) order imbalances are contemporaneously positively (negatively) associated with underlying returns, followed by rapid reversals in the subsequent period.
